newsitem.title: USA: Marvel, Toy Biz and banks reach agreement.
newsitem.headline: Marvel, Toy Biz and banks reach agreement.

text.p: The new management of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc. Thursday reached an agreement with its banks, bondholders and the principal shareholders of Toy Biz Inc. that promises to end months of bitter legal battles and allow the comic giant to emerge from bankruptcy this fall.

Chase Manhattan Bank attorney Thomas Ambro told U.S. Bankruptcy Judge Helen Balick that under the agreement, two entities controlled by investor Carl Icahn will buy the $610 million in secured claims that Marvel owes to Chase and other banks.
A dissident group of Marvel bondholders headed by Icahn last month won a prolonged legal battle to take control of the debtor companies.

The group claims that Marvel controls 70 percent of Toy Biz, which has an exclusive, royalty-free license to make toys based on Marvel's characters, including Spiderman, the X-Men and The Incredible Hulk.
But the toymaker contends that Marvel's stake had been reduced to only 27 percent.
Marvel filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in December.

Under the agreement, Marvel will pay its bank creditors $395 million in cash, proceeds from the sale of Marvel subsidiaries Fleer Corp. and Panini SpA, and warrants to buy 10 percent of a reorganized company which will merge Marvel with Toy Biz.
Fleer and Panini are estimated to fetch between $200 million and $215 million. The new company is expected to have an estimated net equity value of $525 million, Ambro said.

The reorganized company of Marvel and Toy Biz will issue a rights offering that will allow shareholders of Toy Biz, except for Marvel, to buy 49 percent of the merged company and shareholders of Marvel to buy 51 percent.
"It's a great day for Marvel," Marvel's newly installed president, Joseph Calamari, told Reuters.
Calamari said that most of the senior executives of Marvel resigned last week and he will be replacing them soon.
"I've been with Marvel since 1971 and previously owned and ran the company with my partner Jim Galton," he said.
Calamari said that he had spoken with Galton "about doing certain projects" for Marvel.
Fleer President Edmund Feeley and Marvel executive August Liguori were in the courtroom but declined to comment.
The agreement is expected to be made final on July 24, and Balick set Aug. 28 for a hearing on the disclosure statement portion of the plan of reorganization.
Among the parties in the agreement are Isaac Perlmutter and Avi Arad, principal shareholders of Toy Biz.
Marvel's stock edged up 6 cents to $2.375, while Toy Biz shares rose 94 cents to $8.94 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
